list: The official 55 trophies. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them; guides in our own words.

trophies.guide: This is the platinum: it unlocks by itself once the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is nothing to do for it directly. Work through the roadmap in order — story first, then side strands, collectibles, activities and the money cleanup — and it will pop at the end. If one trophy is still missing, the missables view of this guide shows which ones can no longer be earned on this playthrough.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: The platinum unlocks automatically once the last one pops.

trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this trophy comes naturally at the start of the story and cannot be missed. Play through the mission as directed and it unlocks when the mission ends. It is the first story trophy on the road to the platinum.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.guide: Chapter 1 ends when its last mission is complete, and this trophy unlocks with it. There is no extra requirement: just play the story missions in order. Keep an eye on the missable mission trophies in this chapter as you go, since those are the ones that can pass you by.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Play the Chapter 1 story missions in order.

trophies.guide: This trophy marks the end of Chapter 2 and unlocks when the chapter's last mission is done. Play the story missions in order and it comes on its own. Before moving on, check the missables list for any Chapter 2 mission trophy you have not yet earned.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Play the Chapter 2 story missions in order.

trophies.guide: Finishing Chapter 3 unlocks this trophy, with no requirement beyond completing its story missions. It arrives naturally as the story moves into its later half. Use the gap between chapters to clear side strands tied to characters you have met so far.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Play the Chapter 3 story missions in order.

trophies.guide: This is the Chapter 4 completion trophy, earned by finishing the chapter's final story mission. It is unmissable as long as you play the story through. After it, only the final mission stands between you and the story's end, so make sure the missable mission trophies are done before you finish.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Play the Chapter 4 story missions in order.

trophies.guide: The gold story trophy: it unlocks when the final mission of the game is complete. Because it ends the story, earn every missable story trophy first — once the final mission is done, any mission-only trophy you missed may be gone for this playthrough. Which missions those are is listed in this guide's missables view; whether a missed mission can be replayed for its trophy is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Earn the missable story trophies first.

trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, and this trophy is tied to completing it. It is flagged missable because it belongs to a single mission: once that mission is behind you, the window to earn it on this playthrough may be closed. Play the mission when it appears in the story and finish it. Whether mission replay re-opens the trophy is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Trust
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take the Breakfast Run mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a named story mission, and the trophy unlocks when it is complete. It is flagged missable because it is bound to that one mission: finish the heist when the story offers it, and do not leave it for later. Whether the mission can be replayed for the trophy afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take The Cartel Heist mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission, and this trophy comes from finishing it. It is flagged missable because it belongs to that single mission rather than to the story as a whole. Play it when it appears and complete it. Whether mission replay re-opens the trophy is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Family Matters
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take the Child's Play mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission, and this trophy unlocks on completing it. It is flagged missable because the trophy is tied to that one mission: once Headliners is done, the chance to earn it on this playthrough may be gone. Finish the mission when the story offers it. Whether mission replay re-opens the trophy is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take the Headliners mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a named story mission at the airport, and this trophy unlocks when it is complete. It is flagged missable because it belongs to that single mission. Play it when it appears in the story and finish it. Whether mission replay re-opens the trophy is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take the VCIA Takedown mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission, and this trophy unlocks on completing it. It is flagged missable because the trophy is bound to that one mission: finish it when the story offers it. Whether mission replay re-opens the trophy afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take the Operation Savage Glory mission when it appears.

trophies.guide: The gold 100% completion trophy: it unlocks when the game's completion counter reaches 100%, which means finishing the story plus the side content the game counts toward completion. It is the last big goal before the platinum and is usually the final trophy earned. The exact list of what counts toward 100% is not yet confirmed in the game, so work through every stage of this guide's roadmap and watch the in-game completion stat.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Clear the side strands, collectibles and activities in this guide.
Reach 100% completion in the game's stats.

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses and other driving feats the game counts as a stunt — across free roam and missions. There is no single place to do them: stunts build up naturally while driving fast and taking jumps, so this is a long grind best left running in the background of the whole playthrough. It cannot be missed, since stunts can be done any time after the opening.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Drive fast and take jumps whenever you travel.
Keep count in the game's stats until 250 stunts.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type in the game at least once. PlayStation tracks 9 activity types, so the trophy pops once you have sampled all nine — one round, race, game or session of each kind is enough. It cannot be missed: activities stay open after the story. Which nine types the game counts is not yet confirmed in the game, so work through the activity trophies in this guide and this one should pop along the way.
trophies.name: Master of None
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Try one of each activity type: races, fishing, arcade games, drone races, shooting range and the rest.
The trophy pops when the ninth type is tried.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PlayStation tracks 42 challenges, so all 42 need gold. Visit a shooting range, work through its challenges one by one, and replay any that fall short of gold. It cannot be missed: ranges stay open after the story. Gold thresholds per challenge are not yet confirmed in the game, so expect to replay the harder ones.
trophies.name: The Shootist
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Replay any challenge until it earns a gold medal.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations — PlayStation tracks 14 locations, so 14 wins in total, one per place. Find the drone race at each location, win it, and move to the next. It cannot be missed: the races stay open after the story. Where each of the 14 locations sits is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Top Fun
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find a Top Fun drone race location.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — 20 distinct race events, not the same race 20 times. Work through the race types the game offers and win each one once, keeping count as you go. Races stay open after the story, so this cannot be missed. Which races count as different events is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Enter races across the game's race types.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge: take on the fishing challenge against Cal and out-fish him. It is a single head-to-head contest, so the trophy pops the first time you win it. It is not flagged missable, since fishing challenges can be retried, but take it when Cal offers it rather than leaving it. How the challenge is scored is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find the fishing challenge against Cal.

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game from start to finish — any arcade game counts, so pick the one you find easiest. Head to an arcade, start a game and play it through to its end. It cannot be missed: arcades stay open after the story. Which arcade games the game offers is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Play an arcade game through to its end.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy has a strand of side missions, and this trophy unlocks when his final mission is complete. It is flagged missable because it is the end of a character's strand: once Andy's last mission is done, earlier missions in his strand may no longer be available. Play Andy's missions as they appear and finish the last one. Whether the strand can be replayed afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take Andy's missions as they appear.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton has a strand of side missions, and this trophy unlocks when his final mission is complete. It is flagged missable because it closes a character's strand: finish Kenton's missions as they appear, and do not leave his last mission sitting while you push on with the story. Whether the strand can be replayed afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take Kenton's missions as they appear.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy has a strand of side missions, and this trophy unlocks when his final mission is complete. It is flagged missable because it is the end of a character's strand: once the last mission is done, the strand is over. Play Billy's missions as they appear and finish the last one. Whether the strand can be replayed afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take Billy's missions as they appear.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida — eight separate side-story chains given by strangers around the state. Find stranger missions as you explore, play each strand through, and the trophy pops at the eighth completed strand. Strands stay open after the story, so this cannot be missed. Where each stranger stands is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find stranger missions while exploring Leonida.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy has a strand of side missions, and this trophy unlocks when his final mission is complete. It is flagged missable because it closes a character's strand: play Randy's missions as they appear and finish the last one. Whether the strand can be replayed afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take Randy's missions as they appear.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone has a strand of side missions, and this trophy unlocks when his final mission is complete. It is flagged missable because it is the end of a character's strand: once the last mission is done, the strand is over. Play Tyrone's missions as they appear and finish the last one. Whether the strand can be replayed afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take Tyrone's missions as they appear.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida — PlayStation tracks 18 spots, so all 18 are needed. Visit each spot and meditate there, working through the map as you explore. Spots stay open after the story, so this cannot be missed. Where the 18 spots sit is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt down the unique animal Bret asks for and take it. This is a single hunting task for Bret: find the animal, hunt it, and the trophy pops. It is not flagged missable, since the hunt can be retried, but take it when Bret offers it. Which animal it is and where it roams is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Fair Game
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Track and hunt the unique animal.

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards — find the cards scattered around Leonida and finish three sets of them. Cards are a collectible hunt: pick up cards as you explore and keep track of which sets are close to complete. They stay available after the story, so this cannot be missed. How many cards a set holds and where they hide is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 different locations across Leonida. This is a long exploration grind: WAiNK at a location, move on, and repeat until 100 distinct spots are covered. Locations stay open after the story, so it cannot be missed. What counts as a WAiNK location is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's assorted challenge tasks, counted toward a total of 50. Challenges build up across activities and free roam, so play widely and they accumulate on their own. They stay available after the story, so this cannot be missed. Which tasks count as challenges is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Take on challenges across activities and free roam.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the police and escape. It needs your partner present, so start it while you are together, draw the heat, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. It can be retried, so it is not flagged missable. The exact escape conditions are not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Hot Together
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without losing your wanted level — the trick is the opposite of losing the heat: keep the wanted level alive across all three robberies. Hit the first shop, move straight to the second and third, and do not let the stars clear in between. It can be retried, so it is not flagged missable. Which shops count is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Rob two more shops in a row without losing your wanted level.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — drive or encounter 100 distinct vehicles and they are added to your discovered list. This builds up naturally as you explore and steal, borrow or buy cars, bikes, boats and more across Leonida. It cannot be missed, since vehicles stay available after the story. Which vehicles the game counts is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Drive, ride and find vehicles across Leonida.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: In one single use of Combat Focus, take down 5 enemies. Wait for a fight with at least five enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and drop five of them before it ends. It can be retried in any later fight, so it is not flagged missable. Where to find a good five-enemy fight is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find a fight with at least 5 enemies together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down 5 enemies in that one use.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: At VCIA, the airport, make an unscheduled departure — leave by air without a scheduled flight. It is flagged missable because it is a one-off moment at a specific place: take the chance when you are at the airport with a way to fly. Whether the airport stays open for a retry afterwards is not yet confirmed in the game, so do it the first time the opportunity appears.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Make an unscheduled departure by air.

trophies.guide: This trophy's description is a joke about Rhino tanks, and the exact deed it wants is not spelled out — something to do with Rhinos, the tanks. Try driving or fighting in a Rhino and see what the game counts; the trophy pops when the hidden condition is met. It is not flagged missable, since tanks can be found again later. What exactly triggers it is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Use it in a fight or drive until the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — get in, take the goods and get out without any alarm or witness spotting you. It is flagged missable in the sense that a detected attempt fails the condition: a failed run means trying again, so plan the approach, move quietly and leave clean. Which jewelry store and how detection is judged is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one — five separate vault robberies, each ending with a clean getaway. Plan each robbery, grab the vault's contents and lose the heat before the next. Vaults stay open after the story, so this cannot be missed. Where the vaults are is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find a bank vault and rob it.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape afterwards — stop a truck, take its contents and lose the heat. Trucks can be found on the road, so watch for one, hit it, and get away clean. It can be retried, so it is not flagged missable. Where trucks run most often is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find an armored truck on the road.

trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida — PlayStation tracks 52 areas, so all 52 must be visited. Drive, walk and fly through the whole map until every area has been seen. Areas stay open after the story, so this cannot be missed. A map that shows which areas you have visited will help; which 52 areas the game counts is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Travel through every part of the map.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang — PlayStation tracks 9 gangs, so nine robberies, one per gang. Find each gang's illegal operation, rob it, and move to the next gang. Operations stay open after the story, so this cannot be missed. Where each gang's operation sits is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Pest Control
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Find an illegal operation of one gang and rob it.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: On Ocean Beach, enjoy a cocktail with a view — a quiet moment trophy: go to Ocean Beach, get a cocktail and take in the view. It is flagged missable because it is a one-off moment tied to a specific place and activity: do it when you are at Ocean Beach rather than assuming it will wait. Whether the spot stays available later is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Enjoy a cocktail with a view.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight out through the showroom in a big, noisy exit. It is flagged missable because it is a one-off stunt at a specific place: do it when you are in a showroom with a car, rather than leaving it for later. Which showroom counts is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Get a car inside a vehicle showroom.
Smash your way out through the front.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: At the Kolt & Associates bowling alley, follow through — bowl a game there and finish it. It is flagged missable because it is tied to that one specific alley: go there and bowl rather than assuming any alley will do. Whether other alleys count is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Bowl a game and follow through.

trophies.guide: This trophy's description is deliberately vague — a partnership with mass appeal — and the deed it wants is not spelled out. It is flagged missable because it sounds like a one-off partnership moment: when a story or side moment offers a partnership with a crowd watching, take it. What exactly triggers it is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Personal Best
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Watch for a partnership moment with a crowd.

trophies.guide: This trophy is about the choices you make in the game — PlayStation tracks a count of 500 choices, so it pops once you have made enough decisions across the story and side content. It is flagged missable because choices happen during missions and conversations: once a choice is made, it cannot be unmade on that playthrough. Keep playing and choosing; the count builds up on its own. Which choices count toward the 500 is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Make choices in missions and conversations as they come.
The trophy pops as the choice count builds.

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm — succeed at something on your second try. It is flagged missable because it is a one-off moment: fail once, then succeed on the immediate retry. If you pass everything first time, this one can slip past, so when a retry prompt appears after a failure, take it and win on the second attempt. Exactly what must be retried is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? — witness something strange in Leonida, an odd event or encounter the game hides off the beaten path. It is flagged missable because strange events can be one-off: explore odd places and take strange encounters when they appear. What the event is and where it happens is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Trigger the strange event when it appears.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a person with a melee attack from a moving vehicle, bowling them over. It needs a drive-by with a melee weapon rather than a gun, so get a vehicle, get close, and swing as you pass. It can be retried any time, so it is not flagged missable. Which melee weapon works best is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Get a vehicle and a melee weapon.
Drive past someone and hit them with a melee drive-by.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts — pass dirty money through your contacts until a quarter of a million is clean. Marked bills build up from robberies and heists, so keep laundering as you earn them. It cannot be missed: contacts stay open after the story. Which contacts launder bills is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Earn marked bills from robberies and heists.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — buy clothes, weapons, food, cars and anything else the shops sell until the total passes a hundred thousand. Spending builds up naturally across the playthrough, so buy what you need and it will come. It cannot be missed: shops stay open after the story. The running total is tracked in the game's stats.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Buy goods across the game's shops.

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — PlayStation tracks 8 garage properties, so all eight must be bought. Save up, visit each property and buy it; garages give you somewhere to store the vehicles you discover. They stay for sale after the story, so this cannot be missed. Where the eight garages sit is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — find ten vehicles and add each one to the app. Use the vehicles you discover while exploring, register them one by one, and the trophy pops at the tenth. It cannot be missed: the app and the vehicles stay available after the story. How registration works in the app is not yet confirmed in the game.
trophies.name: On the Spot
sources: Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game
steps: Register it to the Scooter Bros app.
